- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes; model reacts too aggressively, peaking too high and then correcting too slowly.
- Late-period forecasts (last 10–15 days) show underestimation, suggesting model fails to capture sustained upward momentum or delayed policy effects.
- Mean reversion bias: model often assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly, missing prolonged trends.
- Forecast lag: model consistently lags true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward corrections.
- High volatility periods (e.g., spikes above 80) are overestimated by model, while low volatility periods are underestimated.
- Model underestimates true price peaks in the 25–30 day window, especially when true prices rise above 82.
